images.title: Take away 40, then 3
images.purpose: Show that taking away a bracket (40 + 3) means taking away both numbers, one after the other.
images.composition: One long horizontal bar for 200, split into three parts, a sketch not to scale, with the equation below.
exact_structure: One bar with dark outline, labelled 200 above its whole length.
Next a vermilion #D55E00 part labelled −40, then a short vermilion part labelled −3, both at the right end.
A reddish purple #CC79A7 bracket under the two vermilion parts labelled (40 + 3).
rejection: a plus sign before 3 in the final line
the bar split into other than 3 parts
images.takeaway: Taking away a bracket of two numbers takes away each of them, so both signs become minus.
images.description: A bar of 200 with 40 and then 3 removed from one end, leaving 157.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text on removing a bracket after a minus sign.
images.teaching_notes: Follow the bar: both small parts leave, none is given back.

image_decisions.why: A bar model shows why the plus inside the bracket becomes a minus.
